clue.text: Material right fool put on view

indicators.note: the right fool is placed on (after) the view, so those pieces follow it

parts.note: to view is to see
a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Someone foolish is put on display while wearing some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like dressing up, and 'view' like a noun, but 'put on' tells you to attach the right fool after the verb for view.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: It used to be very painful

definitions.meaning: in archaic English this word meant greatly

explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb sense meant extremely, as in the Bible's 'sore afraid'; the everyday adjective means aching or tender.

clue.text: You are an outspoken rustic Greek islander

indicators.note: a country speaker in dialect says 'you be' for 'you are', and saying it aloud gives the sound we need

parts.note: in rustic dialect these words come out as 'you be an'

explanation.surface: A blunt country bumpkin from Greece is addressed directly.
explanation.walkthrough: A yokel would say 'you be an', which sounds like the name of someone from Euboea.
explanation.definitionFit: Euboea is a large Greek island, and a native of it is an islander from Greece.

clue.text: Obsessive about scoring individually?

definitions.meaning: playfully, having one's mind on singles, as a batsman scoring one run at a time

explanation.definitionFit: Someone fixated on a single goal is obsessive; whimsically, a mind set on singles cares about scoring one at a time.

clue.text: Such a supportive woman in the Temple

definitions.text: Such a supportive woman in the Temple

parts.words: Such a supportive woman in the Temple
parts.note: not a helpful friend but a carved female figure literally holding up the roof of a Greek temple, as on the Erechtheion in Athens

explanation.definitionFit: Classical architecture uses sculpted female figures in place of columns to bear an entablature.

clue.text: A point to nil, before the end: that'll do

parts.note: a point of the compass, here E for east

indicators.note: the word for zero is cut off just before its final letter

parts.note: nil is zero, nought

explanation.surface: A football score of one-nil late in the game is declared sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A point' is a compass point, not a score; 'before the end' trims the last letter of the word for nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this word means sufficient, the same as declaring that'll do.

clue.text: Pluck the strings

definitions.meaning: catgut used to string instruments such as violins

explanation.definitionFit: Courage is colloquially called guts, and instrument strings were traditionally made of catgut.

clue.text: Not changing gear

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means constant or unvarying; the noun is the regulation outfit worn by soldiers or schoolchildren.

clue.text: Christian virtue fills a need, after a fashion

indicators.note: done in a fashion, i.e. rearranged into a new form, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A Christian virtue supposedly satisfies a need, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' seems to mean 'roughly' but signals an anagram of FILLS A NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity and going without for others is praised as a Christian virtue.

clue.text: Hood household officer put on — here?

parts.note: Robin Hood, the English outlaw of legend
a groom is an officer of the royal household, as in Groom of the Stole

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's servant dresses up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question: where would one put on robes, e.g. a judge or cleric before a ceremony?
explanation.definitionFit: A robing room is the chamber where judges or clergy dress in their official gowns.

clue.text: Ship said to be in German port

indicators.note: said means the word for a ship is heard rather than written

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, a kind of ship

explanation.surface: A vessel is reported to be docked in a German harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' gives KEEL (a barge), which sounds like the Baltic port.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiel is a Baltic harbour city in northern Germany, at the end of the Kiel Canal.

clue.text: Almost 29 in Rome to receive purification, for example

parts.note: 29 across is a prospector of 1849; almost that is forty-nine, written loosely in Roman numerals as one before fifty
lustration is ritual purification

explanation.surface: A Roman almost receives a cleansing ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Romans normally wrote forty-nine as XLIX, but the loose subtractive form, one before fifty, is the crossword's licence here; 'to receive' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is something shown to make a point clear, the same as a picture accompanying a text.

clue.text: Lean over to win the ball

definitions.meaning: to tilt, as a ship does in the wind
in rugby, to push the ball back with the foot in a scrum

explanation.definitionFit: A ship tilting is said to heel; in a rugby scrum a hooker heels the ball backwards to win possession.

clue.text: Sponge money once to meet the fare

parts.note: an angel was an old English gold coin
fare is food served

explanation.surface: Someone cadges old cash to pay for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a verb (to cadge) but is a type of cake; the ANGEL was an old English gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel food is a light, airy kind of sponge cake made with egg whites.

clue.text: Cut wood for utensils

parts.note: to chop is to cut
sticks are pieces of wood

explanation.surface: Someone chops firewood to make kitchen tools.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the pair of slender rods used as eating implements in East Asia.

clue.text: Former servant girl put on about four inches

indicators.note: the girl is put on, i.e. after, the measure

parts.note: a hand is a unit of horse height, roughly four inches
a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman wears heels that add some height.
explanation.walkthrough: A HAND is a horse-measuring unit of four inches.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a female attendant or servant, as used in the Bible.

clue.text: At last, hanging to discourage the terrorist

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word hanging is taken

parts.note: to unman is to sap someone's courage

explanation.surface: Execution is finally proposed as a deterrent to terrorism.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed attacker who shoots people may be a terrorist.

clue.text: Brave pirate's superficial improvement

parts.note: to brave something is to face it
to pirate is to steal, i.e. lift

explanation.surface: A bold buccaneer gets a cosmetic upgrade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' and 'pirate' look like a noun phrase but are both verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally cosmetic surgery, figuratively a cosmetic makeover that changes only the surface.

clue.text: Supine, wavering sort of judge

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge lying on his back is indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: In English law this word describes a junior High Court judge.

clue.text: A very small stretch of speech is naughty

parts.note: A means one, the Roman numeral I
a millimetre, abbreviated mm, is a tiny length
oral means spoken, of speech

explanation.surface: A short bit of talk is judged rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A very small stretch' as one millimetre: I MM.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty can mean wicked or improper, the same as morally wrong.

clue.text: Worker in processing plant needs a head covering

indicators.note: the worker sits inside the plant word

parts.note: a mill is a factory processing raw material
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A factory hand needs a hard hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing plant' looks like the anagram material but is a factory word, and 'Worker' is the crossword's usual insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk scarf worn over the head by Spanish women.

clue.text: Ungainly person, related to Tony?

definitions.meaning: Tony ... is the oafish squire in Goldsmith's play She Stoops to Conquer, so his relatives share his surname

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an awkward lout, and Goldsmith gave that surname to his loutish Tony in She Stoops to Conquer.

clue.text: Manage to assemble a party

parts.note: to make is to assemble
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone organises a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'do' is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by with whatever is available is to manage.

clue.text: Usually mild, but consumed by rage

indicators.note: the consumed word sits beside the rage word

parts.note: temper is anger, rage
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone normally gentle is overtaken by fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by rage' reads as one phrase but is ATE placed by TEMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate is one that is generally mild, without extremes.

clue.text: Lots of men took Mary out

indicators.note: out means the letters of the name are turned out of order

explanation.surface: Several men took a woman out on dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A host of soldiers forms a military force, so it is a great number of men.

clue.text: River causing erosion

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river through Durham in north-east England; gradual damage by friction is wear.

clue.text: Twist copper one way then the other

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R for right, one direction
L for left, the other direction

explanation.surface: A policeman spins round one way and then back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is not a policeman but the metal, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl something is to twist it into a coil or spiral.

clue.text: Gasteropod grows blue

definitions.meaning: a gasteropod is a snail-like mollusc, here a small edible sea snail
a light purplish-blue colour named after a flowering plant

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small edible sea snail and the lavender-blue shade of the evergreen trailing flower.

clue.text: I must leave firm, betrayed

indicators.note: the letter named is taken out of the word for firm

parts.note: solid means firm

explanation.surface: A partner quits the company after being double-crossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective SOLID; removing I gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out, or sell them down the river, is to betray them.

clue.text: Get-rich-quick type needed to repair torn finery

indicators.note: torn clothes must be repaired, i.e. put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A fortune hunter must mend his ripped fancy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1849 California gold rush prospectors are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector in the 1849 California gold rush hoped to become wealthy overnight.
